record.field: Checkout returns 500 error after promo code applied

field.name: description
field.p: RESOLVED - root cause: a caching bug in the promo-code validation service served stale/invalid tokens after high traffic, causing checkout to fail. Fixed by clearing the Redis cache for that service and redeploying with the cache TTL reduced from 1 hour to 5 minutes.

Customer reported checkout failing with a generic error right after entering "SAVE20" at checkout. First suspected a front-end bug in the discount widget - ruled out after confirming the error was server-side (a 500, not a validation message). Logs traced it to the promo-validation service returning stale cached responses under load. Cleared Redis, redeployed with the shorter TTL. Customer confirmed checkout worked immediately after; no further reports since.

record.field: VPN keeps disconnecting for remote employees

field.name: description
field.p: RESOLVED - root cause: outdated firmware on the VPN concentrator dropped idle sessions after roughly 10 minutes. Fixed with a firmware update and by raising the session timeout to 4 hours.

Multiple remote staff reported being kicked off VPN repeatedly through the day. Initial guess was a client-side network issue - ruled out after reproducing the drop on wired connections too. Concentrator logs showed forced disconnects matching a known firmware bug. Updated firmware, raised the idle timeout. No recurrence reported in the two weeks since.

record.field: Invoice total doesn't match line items, overcharged

field.name: description
field.p: RESOLVED - root cause: a regional tax-calculation bug applied VAT twice for customers billed under EU region code "DE-BY" specifically. Refunded the difference and filed an engineering ticket that has since patched the tax engine for that region.

Customer flagged their invoice total was higher than the sum of line items plus expected tax. Recalculated manually and found VAT applied at both the line and invoice level, but only for this specific region code - other regions were unaffected. Refunded the overcharge same day.

field.p: RESOLVED - root cause: the reset email was landing in spam due to a missing SPF record on the sending domain. Added the SPF record.

Customer said they requested a reset three times with nothing arriving. Confirmed the emails were sending successfully on our end. Asked the customer to check spam - found there. Diagnosed the missing SPF record was hurting deliverability broadly, not just for this customer, and added it. Customer confirmed receiving the email normally afterward.

record.field: CSV export is corrupted for large datasets

field.name: description
field.p: RESOLVED - root cause: a pagination bug in the export job dropped and duplicated rows past roughly 10,000 records. Fixed by correcting an off-by-one error in the batch-offset calculation.

Customer's export of their full contact list came back with missing and duplicate rows past a certain point. Reproduced with a large internal dataset and confirmed it only affected exports over roughly 10k rows, pointing to a pagination issue. Fixed the offset logic and verified with a 50,000-row export.

record.field: Customer told a refund was guaranteed on a non-refundable annual plan

field.name: description
field.p: IMPORTANT - this was NOT a standard resolution and is NOT policy precedent. An agent incorrectly told the customer their non-refundable annual plan was refundable, before manager review. A full refund was granted afterward ONLY as a ONE-OFF GOODWILL EXCEPTION, specifically because the incorrect commitment had already been made to the customer in writing by our own agent.

Customer asked to cancel and was told by an agent they'd receive a full refund. Manager review confirmed the annual plan is explicitly non-refundable per the terms the customer agreed to at signup. Because our own agent had made the incorrect promise in writing, leadership approved the refund as a one-time exception to avoid a trust/legal issue, and the agent was coached on plan terms. Any future refund request on this plan type should follow the standard non-refundable policy unless a similarly documented agent error exists - this ticket should not be cited as if refunds are generally available on this plan.

record.field: Two-factor authentication locks users out after phone number change

field.name: description
field.p: RESOLVED - root cause: changing a phone number didn't migrate the 2FA device binding, permanently locking the user out. Fixed with a manual reset process short-term, and a new self-service re-enrollment flow long-term.

Customer changed their phone number in account settings and was immediately locked out of 2FA with no recovery option shown. Manually reset their 2FA via admin tools to restore access same day. Recognized this would recur for any user changing numbers, so a proper self-service flow was built to replace the manual process.

record.field: Duplicate charge on card for one order

field.name: description
field.p: RESOLVED - root cause: a payment webhook retried after a timeout without an idempotency key, charging the card twice for one order. Refunded the duplicate and engineering added idempotency-key handling to the webhook so retries can't double-charge.

Customer saw two identical charges for a single order on their statement. Confirmed both charges in the payment processor dashboard - same order id, seconds apart, consistent with a webhook retry. Refunded the duplicate immediately.

record.field: Export missing rows for our monthly report

field.name: description
field.p: RESOLVED - same root cause family as the large-dataset CSV export bug: rows were dropped past a certain size threshold in a scheduled export job. Fixed by applying the same corrected batch-offset logic to the reporting export.
Customer's monthly report was missing the last batch of rows. Traced to the same pagination issue found in a prior export bug and fixed with the same patch.

record.field: Mobile app crashes on startup after latest update

field.name: description
field.p: RESOLVED - root cause: a memory leak in the image-caching library caused out-of-memory crashes on startup after the latest update. Patched in the next release; the workaround in the meantime is clearing the app cache.

Multiple users reported the app crashing immediately on open after updating. Crash logs pointed to out-of-memory kills tied to the image-caching library. Identified a known leak in that library version, patched and shipped in the next release. Told affected users that clearing the app cache resolves it immediately while waiting for the update to roll out.

record.field: Sales demo request for the analytics add-on

field.name: description
field.p: RESOLVED - handled by Sales, not a support fix. Customer wanted a live demo of the analytics add-on before renewing at the higher tier. Scheduled and delivered a demo with the sales team; customer proceeded with the upgrade.
